s1.content:
Born to a wealthy cloth merchant in Assisi, Francis abandoned a comfortable life after a series of conversions, embracing radical poverty and founding the Franciscan order. He preached to the poor, rebuilt ruined churches, and is remembered for his tenderness toward creation, famously preaching to birds and taming a wolf in legend.

In 1224 he is said to have received the stigmata, the wounds of Christ, while praying on Mount La Verna. He died in 1226 and was canonized just two years later. He is the patron saint of animals, ecology, and Italy.
s1.intercession: St. Francis of Assisi, who found God in poverty and in every creature, teach us to hold this world lightly and to love it truly. Pray for us, that we may walk humbly, live simply, and see the hand of the Creator in all things. Amen.

s2.content:
A French Carmelite nun who died of tuberculosis at twenty-four, Thérèse is known for her "Little Way": the conviction that holiness is found not in grand deeds but in small acts of love done with great fidelity. Her spiritual autobiography, Story of a Soul, was published after her death and became one of the most widely read spiritual works of the modern era.

She was canonized in 1925 and declared a Doctor of the Church in 1997, one of only a handful of women to hold that title.
s2.intercession: St. Thérèse of Lisieux, Little Flower, who found holiness in life’s smallest acts of love, pray for us. Teach us your Little Way, that we may trust God as a child trusts a father, and offer him even our smallest joys and sufferings. Amen.

s3.content:
Born in North Africa, Augustine spent his youth pursuing worldly ambition and Manichean philosophy before his dramatic conversion to Christianity in 386, recounted in his Confessions. He became Bishop of Hippo and one of the most influential theologians in Christian history, shaping doctrines on grace, original sin, and the nature of the Church.

His vast body of writing, including The City of God, continues to be foundational to both Catholic and broader Western thought.
s3.intercession: St. Augustine, who searched restlessly before finding peace in God, pray for all who wrestle with doubt and desire. Obtain for us the grace of a sincere conversion, and hearts that find their rest in the Lord alone. Amen.

s4.content:
An Italian Dominican friar and one of the greatest philosopher-theologians of the Middle Ages, Aquinas sought to reconcile faith with the rediscovered philosophy of Aristotle. His masterwork, the Summa Theologica, systematically addresses questions of God, morality, and the sacraments, and remains central to Catholic theological education.

He is honored as the Angelic Doctor and is the patron saint of students and universities.
s4.intercession: St. Thomas Aquinas, patron of students and scholars, pray for us. Obtain for us a mind eager to seek truth, a will to pursue it honestly, and the grace to hold what we learn always in service of God. Amen.

s5.content:
A Spanish Carmelite nun and mystic, Teresa reformed her order to return it to stricter contemplative observance, founding the Discalced Carmelites alongside St. John of the Cross. Her writings on prayer and the interior life, especially The Interior Castle, remain classics of Christian mysticism.

She was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970, the first woman to receive the title.
s5.intercession: St. Teresa of Ávila, teacher of prayer, pray for us. Help us to persevere through dryness and distraction, and lead us deeper into the interior castle of the soul, where Christ himself dwells. Amen.

s6.content:
A peasant girl from Domrémy, Joan believed she received visions directing her to support Charles VII and lead French forces during the Hundred Years’ War. She led the army to a decisive victory at Orléans in 1429 but was later captured, tried on charges of heresy by a politically motivated court, and burned at the stake in 1431 at nineteen.

She was declared innocent by a posthumous retrial in 1456 and canonized in 1920. She is a patron saint of France and of soldiers.
s6.intercession: St. Joan of Arc, who followed God’s call with unshakable courage, pray for us. Give us your boldness in the face of doubt and opposition, and the humility to submit our own certainty to the will of God. Amen.

s7.content:
A fisherman from Galilee called by Christ to be the "rock" on which the Church would be built, Peter was the leader of the twelve apostles and, by tradition, the first Bishop of Rome. Despite denying Christ three times during the Passion, he was restored and commissioned to feed Christ’s flock, later leading the early Church through its first difficult decades.

He was martyred in Rome under Nero, traditionally crucified upside down at his own request, believing himself unworthy to die as Christ did.
s7.intercession: St. Peter, first among the apostles, pray for the Church and for its shepherds. Obtain for us the grace to rise after our failures as you did, and to love Christ enough to follow him even to the end. Amen.

s8.content:
Once a zealous persecutor of Christians known as Saul, Paul was transformed by an encounter with the risen Christ on the road to Damascus. He became the Church’s greatest missionary, founding communities across the Mediterranean and writing letters that form a large part of the New Testament.

He was martyred in Rome, tradition holds, by beheading, and is honored alongside Peter as a co-founder of the Roman Church.
s8.intercession: St. Paul, apostle to the nations, pray for us. Set our hearts ablaze as yours was on the road to Damascus, and give us courage to proclaim the Gospel in season and out of season. Amen.

s9.content:
Known in his own Gospel as "the disciple whom Jesus loved," John was among the first apostles called and was present at the Transfiguration and the Crucifixion, where Christ entrusted his mother Mary to his care. Tradition credits him with the fourth Gospel, three epistles, and the Book of Revelation.

He is believed to be the only apostle who did not die a martyr’s death, living to old age in Ephesus.
s9.intercession: St. John, beloved disciple, pray for us. Teach us to rest close to the heart of Christ as you did, and to love one another as he has loved us. Amen.

s10.content:
Delivered by Christ from grave affliction, Mary Magdalene became one of his most devoted followers, present at the crucifixion when many others had fled. She was the first witness of the Resurrection and was sent by the risen Christ to announce the news to the apostles, earning her the title "Apostle to the Apostles."

In 2016 Pope Francis raised her liturgical feast to the rank celebrated for the apostles, honoring her unique place in salvation history.
s10.intercession: St. Mary Magdalene, first witness of the Resurrection, pray for us. Obtain for us your same faithful love for Christ, and the courage to proclaim the joy of the Gospel to a world still in need of hope. Amen.

s11.content:
The husband of Mary and foster father of Jesus, Joseph appears in Scripture only through his actions: obeying angelic messages in dreams, protecting the Holy Family in flight to Egypt, and raising Jesus in the trade of carpentry. Scripture records no words of his at all, only quiet, faithful obedience.

He is honored as patron of the universal Church, of fathers, of workers, and of a happy death, having died, by tradition, in the presence of Jesus and Mary.
s11.intercession: St. Joseph, silent and faithful guardian, pray for us. Watch over our families as you watched over the Holy Family, and obtain for us the grace of a peaceful death in the company of Jesus and Mary. Amen.

s12.content:
Though not named in Scripture, St. Anne has been honored since the early Church, by tradition, as the mother of the Virgin Mary and grandmother of Jesus. Devotion to her spread widely through the Middle Ages, and she is invoked especially by mothers, grandparents, and those hoping for children.

She is venerated alongside her husband, St. Joachim, as an example of quiet faithfulness within family life.
s12.intercession: St. Anne, grandmother of our Lord, pray for grandparents and for all who long to pass on the faith to those who come after them. Watch over our families across every generation. Amen.

s13.content:
Born in Nursia, Italy, Benedict withdrew from society as a young man to live as a hermit before founding the monastery of Monte Cassino and writing his famous Rule, which balanced prayer, manual labor, and community life under the motto ora et labora. His moderate, practical approach became the foundation of Western monasticism.

Benedictine houses preserved learning and stability through the upheavals of the early medieval period, earning him the title patron of Europe.
s13.intercession: St. Benedict, father of Western monks, pray for us. Teach us to order our days around prayer and honest work, and to seek God with the same steady discipline you gave to your Rule. Amen.

s14.content:
Captured as a teenager from Roman Britain and enslaved in Ireland, Patrick escaped after six years but later returned as a missionary bishop, having felt called in a vision. He is credited with converting much of pagan Ireland to Christianity, founding churches and monasteries across the island.

The shamrock, by tradition, was his teaching tool for explaining the Trinity, and he remains one of the most beloved patron saints in the world.
s14.intercession: St. Patrick, apostle of Ireland, pray for missionaries and for all who bring the Gospel to unfamiliar and difficult places. Give us your courage to return good for the evil once done to us. Amen.

s15.content:
A Portuguese-born Franciscan friar renowned for his preaching and deep knowledge of Scripture, Anthony was declared a Doctor of the Church for the clarity and power of his sermons. He spent much of his ministry in Padua, Italy, known for his charity to the poor and his gift for reconciling enemies.

He is popularly invoked as the finder of lost items and lost causes, a devotion rooted in a legend of a stolen book miraculously returned.
s15.intercession: St. Anthony of Padua, wonder-worker, pray for us. Help us find what is truly lost — faith grown cold, relationships broken, hope set aside — and restore in us confidence in God’s providence. Amen.

s16.content:
One of the twelve apostles, Jude is traditionally identified as the author of the New Testament epistle bearing his name and is said to have preached the Gospel in Mesopotamia and Persia before being martyred there. Because his name resembled that of the traitor Judas, devotion to him was historically neglected, which by tradition led him to intercede especially readily for those in desperate need.

He is one of the most widely invoked saints in the Church today, particularly in times of hardship thought to be beyond hope.
s16.intercession: St. Jude, patron of hopeless causes, pray for us. In our most desperate hours, when no other help seems near, obtain for us the grace to trust that nothing is beyond the mercy of God. Amen.

s17.content:
A bishop in Asia Minor during the early fourth century, Nicholas became famous for his secret generosity, most notably providing dowries for three poor sisters by tossing gold through their window under cover of night so they would not face destitution. He is said to have attended the Council of Nicaea and defended orthodox teaching on the divinity of Christ.

His legend of quiet, anonymous gift-giving eventually gave rise to the popular figure of Santa Claus.
s17.intercession: St. Nicholas, generous bishop, pray for us. Teach us to give freely and quietly, seeking no praise, and to care for children and the poor as you once did in Myra. Amen.

s18.content:
A soldier in the Roman army, George was martyred under Emperor Diocletian for refusing to renounce his Christian faith, reportedly enduring prolonged torture with steadfast courage before his execution. Little else about his life is reliably documented, but his witness of fidelity under persecution spread rapidly and inspired the popular legend of him slaying a dragon to save a princess, understood as a symbol of his triumph over evil.

He is a patron saint of soldiers, England, and several other nations.
s18.intercession: St. George, valiant martyr, pray for us. Give us courage to stand firm in our faith when it is tested, and to face evil, whatever form it takes, without losing hope in Christ’s victory. Amen.

s19.content:
A captain in the Roman imperial guard, Sebastian was discovered to be secretly Christian and, by tradition, was ordered shot with arrows and left for dead. He survived, was nursed back to health, and confronted the emperor directly about the persecution of Christians, for which he was ultimately clubbed to death.

His survival of the arrows made him a popular subject in art and a patron of soldiers and athletes.
s19.intercession: St. Sebastian, steadfast martyr, pray for us. Give soldiers, athletes, and all who face danger in their work the courage to hold to their faith under pressure and pain. Amen.

s20.content:
The mother of St. Augustine, Monica spent decades praying for her son’s conversion through years of his wandering into worldly ambition and heterodox belief. Her patience and tears, as Augustine himself recorded, were instrumental in his eventual return to the faith and his baptism.

She is remembered as a model of persevering prayer for the conversion of loved ones who seem far from God.
s20.intercession: St. Monica, patient mother, pray for us. Hear the prayers of every parent who weeps for a child astray, and obtain for them the same steadfast hope that carried you through years of waiting. Amen.

s21.content:
A brilliant and famously irritable scholar, Jerome dedicated much of his life to translating the Bible from Hebrew and Greek into Latin, producing the Vulgate, which remained the Church’s standard biblical text for over a thousand years. He lived for decades as a hermit and monk near Bethlehem, immersed in study and controversy alike.

He is honored as a Doctor of the Church and the patron of biblical scholars and translators.
s21.intercession: St. Jerome, lover of Scripture, pray for us. Give us your hunger for the word of God, and remind us, as you often said, that ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ. Amen.

s22.content:
A Roman governor unexpectedly acclaimed bishop of Milan by popular demand while still an unbaptized catechumen, Ambrose became one of the most influential churchmen of his age, instructing Augustine and famously standing up to emperors on matters of Church authority. His eloquent preaching and hymn-writing shaped Western liturgical music.

He is honored as a Doctor of the Church, remembered for his courage in defending the Church’s independence from imperial power.
s22.intercession: St. Ambrose, fearless bishop, pray for us. Give Church leaders your courage to speak truth to power, and give us all a love for the beauty of the liturgy that you helped shape. Amen.

s23.content:
A Spanish soldier wounded in battle, Ignatius underwent a profound conversion during a long recovery, later founding the Society of Jesus (the Jesuits) to serve the Church through education, missionary work, and spiritual direction. His Spiritual Exercises, a structured method of prayer and discernment, remain widely used today.

He emphasized finding God "in all things," bringing contemplative depth into active, engaged life in the world.
s23.intercession: St. Ignatius of Loyola, pray for us. Teach us to discern God’s will in the ordinary movements of our hearts, and to seek him not only in prayer but in all our daily work. Amen.

s24.content:
A close companion of St. Ignatius of Loyola and one of the first Jesuits, Francis Xavier became one of history’s most extensive Christian missionaries, traveling across India, Southeast Asia, and Japan to preach the Gospel, reportedly baptizing tens of thousands of converts. He died within sight of mainland China, still hoping to enter it as a missionary.

He is honored as a patron of foreign missions alongside St. Thérèse of Lisieux.
s24.intercession: St. Francis Xavier, tireless missionary, pray for us. Give missionaries strength for the journey to unfamiliar lands, and set our own hearts on fire to carry Christ to those who have not yet heard of him. Amen.

s25.content:
Known as the Curé of Ars for the small French parish he served for over forty years, John Vianney struggled academically as a seminarian yet became one of history’s most sought-after confessors, reportedly spending up to sixteen hours a day hearing confessions as pilgrims traveled from across Europe to see him.

He is the patron saint of parish priests, remembered for his humility, penance, and tireless availability to souls in need.
s25.intercession: St. John Vianney, patron of priests, pray for all who serve as confessors and pastors. Give them your patience and love for souls, and give penitents the courage to seek mercy without fear. Amen.

s26.content:
An Italian Capuchin friar who bore the visible wounds of Christ’s stigmata for roughly fifty years, Padre Pio became one of the twentieth century’s most sought-after spiritual figures, drawing enormous crowds to his monastery in San Giovanni Rotondo. He spent long hours each day hearing confessions and was reported by many to possess gifts of healing and spiritual insight.

He was canonized in 2002 and remains one of the most widely venerated saints of the modern era.
s26.intercession: St. Padre Pio, who bore the wounds of Christ, pray for us. Help us to unite our own sufferings to his, and to seek healing and mercy with the same trust you showed throughout your life. Amen.

s27.content:
A Polish Franciscan friar imprisoned at Auschwitz, Kolbe volunteered to die in place of a fellow prisoner, a husband and father, who had been selected for starvation as punishment for another inmate’s escape. He led his fellow condemned prisoners in prayer during their final days and was ultimately killed by lethal injection.

He is honored as a martyr of charity, and the man he saved was present at his canonization in 1982.
s27.intercession: St. Maximilian Kolbe, martyr of charity, pray for us. Give us even a portion of your willingness to lay down our lives for another, and strengthen all who suffer persecution for their faith. Amen.

s28.content:
A Polish nun of humble background and little formal education, Faustina reported visions of Jesus who asked her to spread devotion to his Divine Mercy. Her spiritual diary, recorded at the direction of her confessors, became the foundation for the Divine Mercy devotion and image now found throughout the world.

She was canonized in 2000 by Pope John Paul II, her fellow Pole, who also established Divine Mercy Sunday on her recommendation.
s28.intercession: St. Faustina, apostle of Divine Mercy, pray for us. Help us to trust in Jesus as you did, and to carry his message of mercy to a world so often convinced it is beyond forgiveness. Amen.

s29.content:
Born Karol Wojtyła in Poland, he survived Nazi occupation and Communist rule before being elected pope in 1978, the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries. His nearly twenty-seven-year pontificate was marked by extensive world travel, a central role in the fall of Communism in Eastern Europe, and a particular closeness to young people through World Youth Day.

He survived an assassination attempt in 1981 and later personally forgave the man who shot him. He was canonized in 2014.
s29.intercession: St. John Paul II, pray for us. Give young people the courage you so often called for, to "be not afraid," and help all of us to forgive as freely as you forgave your own attacker. Amen.

s30.content:
Born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu in what is now North Macedonia, Mother Teresa spent nearly two decades teaching before feeling called to serve "the poorest of the poor" on the streets of Calcutta. She founded the Missionaries of Charity, which grew into a worldwide order caring for the dying, the abandoned, and the destitute.

Her later revealed private writings disclosed decades of profound spiritual darkness borne quietly alongside her public work. She was canonized in 2016.
s30.intercession: St. Teresa of Calcutta, pray for us. Teach us to see Christ in the poorest and most overlooked, and to keep serving faithfully even when, like you, we feel no consolation in our faith. Amen.

s31.content:
Married young to a violent and unfaithful husband, Rita endured an eighteen-year marriage before his death, and later lost both her sons as well. She then entered an Augustinian convent, where she lived a life of deep penance and, by tradition, received a wound on her forehead resembling a thorn from Christ’s crown.

She is widely invoked as a patron of difficult marriages, widows, and seemingly impossible or hopeless situations.
s31.intercession: St. Rita of Cascia, patron of impossible causes, pray for us. You who bore great suffering within your own family, intercede for all in difficult marriages and troubled homes, that they may find peace. Amen.

s32.content:
A poor, sickly fourteen-year-old girl in Lourdes, France, Bernadette reported eighteen apparitions of a "beautiful lady" who identified herself as the Immaculate Conception, revealing a spring of water that became famous for reported healings. She endured intense scrutiny and skepticism from both civil and Church authorities before her visions were officially recognized.

She later entered religious life and asked to be forgotten, living quietly until her death from illness at thirty-five.
s32.intercession: St. Bernadette, humble seer of Lourdes, pray for the sick and for all who seek healing in body or spirit. Teach us your simplicity of faith before the mysteries God chooses to reveal. Amen.

s33.content:
An Italian laywoman and Dominican tertiary, Catherine experienced profound mystical union with Christ from a young age and became an influential voice in Church affairs, most famously persuading Pope Gregory XI to return the papacy from Avignon to Rome. Unable to read or write until later in life, she dictated hundreds of letters and a major mystical work, The Dialogue.

She was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1970, alongside Teresa of Ávila.
s33.intercession: St. Catherine of Siena, pray for us. Give us your fearless honesty in speaking truth to those in authority, and your deep union of heart with Christ that made such courage possible. Amen.

s34.content:
A wealthy Episcopalian widow with five children, Elizabeth Ann Seton converted to Catholicism after encountering the faith in Italy, a decision that cost her much of her social standing and family support. She founded the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph, establishing the first free Catholic school for girls in America and pioneering the American parochial school system.

She was canonized in 1975, the first person born in the United States to be declared a saint.
s34.intercession: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton, pray for us. Give widowed and single parents your resourcefulness and faith, and inspire Catholic educators to serve children with the same devotion you brought to your schools. Amen.

s35.content:
A Spanish priest troubled by the spread of heresy in southern France, Dominic founded the Order of Preachers, known as the Dominicans, dedicated to rigorous study and public preaching in defense of Catholic doctrine. He insisted his friars live in poverty so their preaching would be credible to those they hoped to reach.

Devotion to the Rosary has long been associated with Dominic and his order, though the precise history of that connection is debated by historians.
s35.intercession: St. Dominic, father of preachers, pray for us. Give us a hunger for truth and the courage to speak it plainly, and help us to pray the Rosary with the depth your order has long taught. Amen.

s36.content:
A French priest who once experienced enslavement himself before his ordination, Vincent de Paul devoted his life to organizing systematic care for the poor, the sick, and abandoned children, founding the Congregation of the Mission and, with St. Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity. His approach professionalized and expanded Catholic charitable work well beyond his own lifetime.

His name is carried today by the worldwide Society of St. Vincent de Paul, which continues direct service to the poor.
s36.intercession: St. Vincent de Paul, pray for us. Give us your practical love for the poor, one that moves beyond good intentions into real, organized, patient service. Amen.

s37.content:
Born Isabel Flores de Oliva in Lima, Peru, Rose lived a life of intense penance and prayer while supporting her family through embroidery and gardening, resisting pressure to marry in order to consecrate her life to Christ. She cared for the sick and poor of her city from a small hermitage built in her family’s garden.

Canonized in 1671, she was the first person born in the Americas to be declared a saint.
s37.intercession: St. Rose of Lima, pray for us. Give young people facing pressure to abandon their calling the same firm resolve you showed, and a heart devoted to serving the poor of their own city. Amen.

s38.content:
Born in Lima to a Spanish nobleman and a freed Black woman, Martin faced discrimination for his mixed heritage yet was admitted to the Dominican order, where he served as a lay brother caring for the sick, the poor, and even animals. He was known for extraordinary humility, insisting on the lowliest tasks despite reports of remarkable spiritual gifts.

He was canonized in 1962 and is honored as a patron of racial harmony and social justice.
s38.intercession: St. Martin de Porres, pray for us. Teach us your humility in choosing the lowest place, and your tender care for the sick, the poor, and all creatures, without regard for their standing in the eyes of the world. Amen.

s39.content:
Born to a Mohawk father and Christian Algonquin mother in what is now New York State, Kateri survived smallpox as a child, which left her partially blind and scarred. She converted to Christianity as a young woman against significant opposition from her community, eventually fleeing to a Christian settlement in Canada, where she lived a life of intense prayer and penance until her death at twenty-four.

She was canonized in 2012, the first Native American to be declared a saint.
s39.intercession: St. Kateri Tekakwitha, Lily of the Mohawks, pray for us. Give indigenous peoples and converts facing opposition from their own communities the same courage and peace you found in following Christ. Amen.

s40.content:
Named in Scripture as "one of the chief princes" and the great protector who contends against the forces of evil, Michael appears in the Book of Daniel, the Letter of Jude, and the Book of Revelation, where he leads the heavenly hosts against the dragon. His name, meaning "Who is like God?", is understood as his answer to Satan’s pride.

He is venerated as the protector of the Church and is traditionally invoked for defense against spiritual and physical danger.
s40.intercession: St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle. Be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil, and by the power of God, cast into hell Satan and all the evil spirits who prowl about the world seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.
